## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/01.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Overview of COVID-19
Academic Impact Study</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Introduction
Components
• Provide context of COVID-19 in Indiana &amp; nationally
• Identify state &amp; federal expectations
• Acknowledge “pre-existing” conditions
• Indicate purpose/s of study
• Understand academic impact of COVID-19 to provide intentional supports &amp;
resources
• NOT accountability</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Research Questions
• Question #1: Who are the students in Indiana?
• Overall description of student population.
• Overall description of students for whom assessment data has been collected. Who do we
not have data?

• Question #2: To what extent did COVID-19 disruptions impact student
academic performance &amp; learning outcomes?
• Overall academic impact
• Disparities in academic impact
• Content area academic impact (E/La &amp; math; English language proficiency)

• Question #3: What is the anticipated academic recovery time based on
the experienced COVID-19 disruptions?</div>
```

::: notes
```{=html}
Question #1: discuss Adam’s work to ensure “apples to apples” comparisons in study<br>
Question #2: reinforce that this question will address state-level; publishing information on corporation level has strong potential to turn into Accountability
```
:::

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Research Questions
Areas of Consideration
• Student racial/ethnic subgroup
• Special education status
• English learner status
• Poverty status
• Community type (urban, suburban, rural)
• School type (traditional public, charter, nonpublic/choice)
• Mode of instruction
• Student attendance</div>
```

::: notes
```{=html}
Are there areas not included here that leadership would like to consider?
```
:::

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Data Sources
Components
• Assessment data
• ILEARN for E/La &amp; math (grades 3-8)
• WIDA ACCESS 2.0 for English learners (K-12)
• NWEA MAP interim for E/La &amp; math (grades 1-10)
• Population data
• Ed-Fi Attendance &amp; Student Demographic data
• Poverty index data
• Technology data
• Annual technology plan</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Data Sources
Notes on NWEA MAP data
• Received data from Fall 2020-2021 and Winter 2020-2021 administration
windows
• Data consisted primarily of language arts and mathematics data for Grades
• Statewide participation approached/exceeded 40% in all grades except 9 &amp; 10

Notes on High School data
• Limited interim assessment data makes it difficult to conduct sufficient
analysis of grades 9-12
• Changes in ISTEP+ 10 administration introduce problems for comparison of
status &amp; growth.</div>
```

::: notes
```{=html}
NOTE: data limitations at high school level
```
:::

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/08.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Methodology
Components
• Consultation with Indiana Technical Advisory Committee
• Measurement of academic impact
• Status: comparison of proficiency level from year to year
• Growth: comparison of growth (cohort referenced and baseline) from year to year
• Measurement of recovery time
• No Impact
• Minor Impact
• Moderate Impact
• Significant Impact</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/09.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Methodology
Measurement of Academic Impact – NWEA Interim
Assessment
• Consider status &amp; growth comparisons of the following:
• Fall 19/20 to Fall 20/21
• Fall 20/21 to Winter 20/21
• Winter 19/20 to Winter 20/21
• Fall 20/21 to Spring 20/21
• Winter 20/21 to Spring 20/21
• Spring 18/19 to Spring 20/21</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/10.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Methodology
Measurement of Academic Impact – Summative
Assessment
• Consider status &amp; growth comparisons of the following:
• Spring 2019 to Spring 2021

Measurement of Academic Impact – WIDA ACCESS 2.0
Assessment
• Consider status &amp; growth comparisons of the following:
• Winter 2020 to Winter 2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/11.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Findings
Components
• Enrollment, attendance, and mode of instruction, broken out by sub-
topics
• Experienced learning loss, broken out by sub-topics
• Disparities in learning loss, broken out by sub-topics
• Content area learning loss, broken out by sub-topics
• Assigned recovery time “impact” statuses, broken out by sub-topics</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/12.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Conclusion &amp; Recommendations
Components
• Summary of COVID-19 academic impact
• Policy &amp; support interventions
• Theory of action—identify purpose/priorities/goals for accelerating
learning
• Divide into short-term/immediate need &amp; long-term strategy based
on establishment of “baseline” and current “impact” category
• Ensure equity considerations of “pre-existing conditions” are
considered in any strategic planning</div>
```

::: notes
```{=html}
For policy &amp; support interventions: cross-departmental collaboration to develop and create appropriate response to ensure support is provided to school corporations<br>
While we will have the ability to look at data at the corporation level, we strongly recommend that such information be used for internal/deliberative purposes only—we do not want this report to be used as a replacement for accountability in this “off” year
```
:::

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/13.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Timeline
Components
• May/June 2021
• Receive summative assessment &amp; WIDA ACCESS 2.0 assessment results in May/June
• Conduct status &amp; growth analyses on summative and EL proficiency assessment results
• June/July 2021
• Finalize report &amp; share findings with DOE leadership &amp; relevant DOE teams to align
findings with DOE supports and guidance
• August 2021
• Share report with policymakers/stakeholders
• Publish report &amp; present findings/DOE’s strategic response</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/14.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Communication
Questions
• Does this research plan align with the goals and priorities
held by leadership for the “learning loss” study?
• Are there any areas of concern with this research plan? Are
there any areas that are missing from this research plan?
• How does this study fit into the overall mission of
leadership?
• Which divisions/directors need to be included in review of
findings &amp; development of strategic response plan</div>
```
